answer: New identities must stand in a real street. LoRa beacons on city infrastructure broadcast signed challenges, and the newcomer's radio must answer in under ninety milliseconds before the registry stamps it. The beacons hide where nobody looks: a willow planter, a junction box, a market sign. No two beacons share a wall, so a basement of clones cannot cover two blocks. One identity needs a radio and a walked block; ten thousand is a sonnet of logistics nobody finishes. A gale hits one alley at a time; a sybil creator hits the same way — the city keeps more corners than any factory can rent.
